findings.evidence: `pkg/domain/infosync/info.go:612-629` now does `continue` when `info.StmtCtx.IsDDLJobInQueue` is true, which skips both `CurTxnStartTS` and `info.CursorTracker.RangeCursor(...)` for that session. Cursor snapshots are tracked independently of the session txn: `pkg/session/session.go:2482-2490` creates a cursor handle with `StartTS` and then calls `finishStmt(...)` to commit/cleanup, so the cursor can outlive the session txn. TiDB supports running other statements while cursor fetch is active (`pkg/server/tests/cursor/cursor_test.go:219-244` interleaves `rows.Next(...)` with `conn.QueryContext(...)`), so a connection can have active cursors while executing a DDL statement. DDL sets the flag after job submission (`pkg/ddl/executor.go:6769-6771`) and resets at stmt end (`pkg/executor/ddl.go:155-158`), meaning long DDL waits are exactly when cursor StartTS can be omitted from minStartTS reporting.
findings.fix: In `InfoSyncer.ReportMinStartTS`, skip only the DDL session’s `CurTxnStartTS` contribution, but still always scan `CursorTracker.RangeCursor(...)` (and any other snapshot-holding sources) even when `IsDDLJobInQueue` is true. Add a regression test: open a cursor (detached record set) on a connection, then run a long DDL on the same connection (after job enqueue) and assert the cursor `StartTS` still contributes to reported `minStartTS`.
findings.impact: A session with an active server-side cursor can execute a long-running DDL; while `IsDDLJobInQueue` is true, the cursor’s snapshot `StartTS` is not reported to PD as part of minStartTS. This can allow GC safepoint to advance past an in-use cursor snapshot (within `GCMaxWaitTime`), leading to cursor `FETCH` failing later with "GC life time is shorter than transaction duration" (or other snapshot-too-old errors).
findings.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed up to `upstream/master` (e.g. `upstream/master:pkg/domain/infosync/info.go` still `continue`s before cursor scanning; later commit `f7fe4a6843` only makes `IsDDLJobInQueue` atomic, keeping the same skip semantics).
findings.verify: Repro scenario: (1) open a server-side cursor (prepared stmt with cursor) so `cursorTracker` holds a `StartTS`; (2) on the same connection, start a long DDL that reaches “job submitted” (so `IsDDLJobInQueue` becomes true) and blocks (use a DDL failpoint to pause after enqueue); (3) ensure `ReportMinStartTS` still reports `minStartTS <= cursor StartTS` during the DDL wait, and cursor fetch continues without GC-snapshot-too-old errors after the DDL finishes.
findings.what: `ReportMinStartTS` ignores entire sessions when `StmtCtx.IsDDLJobInQueue` is true, which also ignores active cursor snapshot `StartTS` on that connection; this can let GC safepoint advance past an in-use cursor snapshot if the same connection runs a long DDL while a cursor remains open.

subject: domain: ignore DDL session when calculating the min startTs (#62607)
summary: This commit changes `InfoSyncer.ReportMinStartTS` to skip sessions with `StmtCtx.IsDDLJobInQueue` (intended to avoid DDL-in-TXN blocking minStartTS/GC), and adds an executor/staticrecordset integration test covering that scenario.
